raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Split from #41994 as requested in review: the batch < 64 part. The other parts are #42280 (`MinFreeSlotsDelayer`) and #42281 (DSpark verify width, closed in favor of compact verify).

## Motivation

With overlap scheduling and speculative decoding on HIP, `FutureMap.resolve_seq_lens_cpu` and `resolve_mixed_spec_tails` block the host on the previous forward's publish event (`publish_ready.synchronize()`, #26672). DSpark publishes after verify and accept, near the end of the step, so the GPU idles while the host prepares the next batch: event-timed on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X, 0.65 ms of an 8.9 ms batch-1 cycle.

The host sync exists because `Event.wait()` on the separate schedule stream is slower still: a device wait pending in another HIP queue while a graph runs slows every dispatch of that graph (on MI355X a 512-kernel graph takes 1541 us instead of 853 us with such a wait pending). In the same timing, replacing the sync with that wait alone removed 0.50 ms of the idle but made the verify graph 1.21 ms slower.

`needs_cpu_seq_lens=False` alone does not remove this sync: on HIP the sync runs before the flag is checked, and the GPU gather of `new_seq_lens_buf` right after it needs the publish ordering in any case. The DeepSeek-V4.1 HIP backend already sets the flag to False (#41308).

## Modifications

On HIP with overlap scheduling and speculative decoding, without pipeline parallelism, and when no attention backend of the step keeps the CPU seq_lens mirror (`needs_cpu_seq_lens=False`), the scheduler runs on the forward stream (`Scheduler.schedule_on_forward_stream`, decided once in `init_overlap`, applied in `run_event_loop`), and `FutureMap(same_queue_publish=True)` waits on the publish event in-queue with `Event.wait()` instead of blocking the host. Stream order carries the forward-to-schedule dependencies.

These cases keep the current path:

- A backend that keeps the CPU mirror, such as aiter (the HIP default): the mirror is pulled with `.cpu()`, which on the forward stream waits for the whole forward (for EAGLE, including draft_extend) instead of the publish. Without this exclusion, Llama-3.1-8B + EAGLE3 on aiter lost 2.35% of batch-1 decode throughput (Table 3).
- Overlap without speculation: it has no publish wait, so the separate schedule stream keeps overlapping batch preparation.
- Pipeline parallelism, which runs its own event loop (`event_loop_pp`) and streams.

CUDA is unchanged.

No new unit test: the change only moves where the publish wait runs, so its observable effect is timing. A CPU test could only restate the gate or assert a mocked `Event` call, which `.claude/rules/unit-test-admission.md` does not admit. The AMD speculative CI tests use the triton backend (`needs_cpu_seq_lens=False`) and run the new path; the aiter EAGLE3 runs below cover the excluded one.

## Accuracy Tests

Same servers as the speed tests; every request greedy.

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Low-Latency cell: GSM8K 64 (C = 64) main 63/64 and 62/64, this PR 62/64 and 62/64; 8/8 retrieval probes on every server.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, High-Throughput cell: GSM8K 64 (C = 64) main 61/64 and 63/64, this PR 61/64 and 61/64.
- Llama-3.1-8B + EAGLE3, aiter and triton: 8/8 retrieval probes on every server; GSM8K 64 54/64 on every server with identical answers (scored by the last number; the model does not write `#### n`); batch-1 outputs token-identical across all servers.
- AMD CI tests on this head, in the ROCm 10 CI image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm10-mi35x-20261014` on MI355X through `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_exec.sh`: `test_basic_sanity_eagle3`, `test_dflash`, `test_frozen_kv_mtp`, `test_spec_standalone_extra`, `test_eagle_worker_v2_topk1_fastpath`, `test_build_eagle_tree`, `test_resolve_swa_kv_pool`, `test_adaptive_speculative` and `test_eagle_dp_attention` (4 GPUs) pass, and the overlap-related unit tests pass (188 passed, 184 subtests).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X (gfx950). Image: `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.21-rocm720-mi35x-20261012`, the DeepSeek-V4.1 cookbook image (sglang `1a553927b0`, AITER `e7d2453f`). main is the image as shipped; this PR is the same image with this PR's three files (`1a553927b0` plus this diff). Fresh server per run in ABBA order, real acceptance, radix cache flushed before every measured request or batch, no profiler during timing, the other GPUs of the node idle (amd-smi at 1 Hz). Intervals: 95% hierarchical bootstrap.

Table 1: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash `dba1be0a`, MI355X cookbook Low-Latency cell (TP2/EP1, DSpark block 5, decode graphs up to 64, cookbook env and flags).

| Workload | Metric | main | This PR | Change (95% CI) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Batch 1, 4 real-text 4K prompts x 24 per server, 1024 tokens | decode tok/s | 368.7 | 389.7 | +5.68% [+4.54, +6.90] |
| | wall per verify | 8.67 ms | 8.27 ms | |
| Batch 8, distinct real-text 4K prompts, 1024 tokens | verify cycles/s | 61.0 | 63.1 | +3.36% [+2.50, +4.73] |
| Batch 32 | verify cycles/s | 34.5 | 35.0 | +1.63% [+1.21, +2.09] |
| Batch 64 | verify cycles/s | 24.1 | 24.4 | +1.08% [+0.97, +1.18] |

On the earlier TP4/EP4 cell with graphs up to 128 (main `71584b62c0`, comment above), batch 1 was +4.81% [+3.79, +5.86].

Table 2: the MI355X High-Throughput cell (TP2/EP1, DSpark, decode graphs up to 128, 128 running requests), three bursts of 256 distinct 4K prompts x 1024 tokens per server.

| Metric | main | This PR | Change (95% CI) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| output tok/s | 3949 | 3991 | +1.09% [-0.73, +3.93] |
| TPOT median | 26.5 ms | 26.5 ms | +0.02% [-1.57, +2.05] |

One main burst ran slow (3712 tok/s, the first burst of the last server); without it the change is +0.2%. No change either way at this load.

Table 3: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct + `lmsys/sglang-EAGLE3-LLaMA3.1-Instruct-8B` (fp16, 3 steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens), TP1, batch 1 as in Table 1. aiter keeps the CPU mirror and is excluded by this PR; the aiter row measures the forward-stream schedule without the exclusion. (bf16 fails the draft graph capture on this image with and without this PR.)

| Attention backend | needs_cpu_seq_lens | main | Forward-stream schedule | Change (95% CI) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| aiter (default) | True | 93.6 tok/s | 91.4 tok/s | -2.35% [-2.58, -1.87], excluded by this PR |
| triton | False | 198.9 tok/s | 198.3 tok/s | -0.28% [-1.15, +0.60] |

What the host sync costs depends on the work after the publish. DSpark publishes at the end of the step. EAGLE publishes before draft_extend, so with 3 steps the current path already prepares the next batch while draft_extend runs (the neutral triton row); with the CI config of `test_basic_sanity_eagle3` (1 step, 2 draft tokens, triton), the single-batch `sglang:fwd_occupancy` median is 96.1% on this PR and 91.8% on main (two PR runs, one main run between them; p10 96.0% vs 89.4%).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.
